root_cause.text: The LoongArch BPF JIT compiler failed to extend the arguments of native kfunc calls to comply with the LoongArch ABI calling conventions.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check for `BPF_PSEUDO_KFUNC_CALL` in `build_insn()` and introduces the `emit_abi_ext()` helper to perform proper sign or zero extension on the argument registers before the native call is executed.

    LoongArch: BPF: Adjust the parameter of emit_jirl()
    
    The branch instructions beq, bne, blt, bge, bltu, bgeu and jirl belong
    to the format reg2i16, but the sequence of oprand is different for the
    instruction jirl. So adjust the parameter order of emit_jirl() to make
    it more readable correspond with the Instruction Set Architecture manual.

Author: Tiezhu Yang <yangtiezhu@loongson.cn>
Date:   Wed Oct 12 16:36:20 2022 +0800

    LoongArch: Add BPF JIT support
    
    BPF programs are normally handled by a BPF interpreter, add BPF JIT
    support for LoongArch to allow the kernel to generate native code when
    a program is loaded into the kernel. This will significantly speed-up
    processing of BPF programs.
    
    Co-developed-by: Youling Tang <tangyouling@loongson.cn>
    Signe
bic_trace_step.reason: In the BPF_JMP | BPF_CALL case of build_insn (lines 608-622), the JIT compiler simply resolves the function address, loads it into a temporary register, and performs a jump-and-link (jirl) instruction. It does not perform any sign-extension or zero-extension on the argument registers (BPF_REG_1 to BPF_REG_5, mapped to LOONGARCH_GPR_A0 to LOONGARCH_GPR_A4) to comply with the LoongArch ABI calling conventions for kfunc calls, which requires 32-bit arguments to be properly extended.
